coffee-instant-pre-lightened-and-pre-swe.title: Instant coffee, pre‑lightened and pre‑sweetened with low‑calorie sweetener, reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: Instant coffee that has been pre‑lightened and pre‑sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener is a convenient beverage that dissolves quickly in hot water. It undergoes an initial roast, followed by a lightening process and sweetening with a sugar substitute, reducing calories without sacrificing taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Instant coffee was invented in the early 20th century and quickly gained popularity for its speed of preparation.
Pre‑lightening reduces bitterness, giving the coffee a smoother, more pleasant flavor.
Low‑calorie sweeteners such as sucralose or stevia are commonly used in diet products.
The packaging is usually hermetically sealed, extending shelf life to 2‑3 years.
Instant coffee retains most aromatic compounds but may have a slightly different flavor profile compared to freshly ground coffee.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Boosts energy
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, increasing alertness and concentration.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The use of a low‑calorie sweetener keeps the drink’s calorie count minimal, useful for weight management.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine can slightly increase metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee provides small amounts of vitamins B2, B3, and B5, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after caffeine intake.

items.title: Sweetener tolerance
items.content: Certain sugar substitutes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Possible allergies
items.content: Rarely, allergic reactions to flavorings or additives may occur.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can increase stomach acidity, which may be problematic for people with gastritis.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Place 1‑2 teaspoons of the product into 200 ml of hot (but not boiling) water and stir until fully dissolved. Milk, cream, or spices can be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the package tightly sealed to prevent moisture ingress.

egg-omelet-or-scrambled-egg-with-cheese-.title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese, meat and tomatoes, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs cooked without added oil, combined with cheese, lean meat (such as ham or chicken) and fresh tomatoes. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while cheese and meat add flavor and additional nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable and versatile foods.
Cooking without added fat preserves the natural taste of ingredients and reduces calorie content.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after heating.
The cheese used is usually low‑fat, lowering saturated fat levels.
The dish is quick to prepare, making it a popular breakfast option.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs supply all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, riboflavin and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The meal provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes deliver an antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor yolk intake.

items.title: Sodium in cheese and meat
items.content: Low‑fat cheese and processed meats can still contain added salt, which is relevant for hypertension.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs, add diced tomatoes, cheese and pre‑cooked or baked meat. Cook on a dry non‑stick pan, stirring until the mixture sets. Fresh herbs can be added for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best eaten immediately. If needed, store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a pan without adding oil.

egg-substitute-omelet-scrambled-or-fried.title: Egg substitute, omelet, scrambled, or fried, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Egg substitute is a ready‑to‑use product that mimics the functional properties of eggs in cooking. It can be used to make omelets, scrambled eggs, or fried dishes, with added fat to provide the desired texture and flavor similar to traditional egg preparations.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The substitute is often made from plant proteins such as soy or pea, combined with vegetable oils.
It is suitable for vegetarians but not always for vegans if gelatin is present.
Many versions are fortified with B‑group vitamins that are naturally found in eggs.
The added fat is usually a plant oil (e.g., sunflower or rapeseed oil).
Egg substitute is widely used in the food industry for large‑scale production without the risk of bacterial contamination.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Unlike chicken eggs, the substitute contains no cholesterol, which may benefit people monitoring their lipid levels.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: It provides a complete set of amino acids needed for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Vitamin‑fortified
items.content: Often enriched with vitamin D, B12 and riboflavin to mimic the nutritional profile of eggs.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: Requires no beating, stores longer than fresh eggs, and cooks quickly.

items.title: Supports special diets
items.content: Can be used in diets that limit animal products, provided it is free of animal‑derived ingredients.

items.title: Allergy to soy/pea proteins
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the plant proteins used.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Added vegetable fat increases calorie density, so portion control is advised for those watching intake.

items.title: Additive sensitivity
items.content: Certain formulations contain emulsifiers or stabilizers that may not be suitable for people sensitive to food additives.

items.title: Not vegan-friendly
items.content: If gelatin or other animal‑derived ingredients are present, the product is not suitable for vegans.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The substitute can be prepared as an omelet, scrambled eggs, or fried dishes by adding spices, vegetables, and herbs. For an omelet, whisk the product with a little water, then cook in a lightly oiled pan until golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in the original packaging. Once opened, use within 5‑7 days. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 3 months.

green-beans-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked.title: Green beans, canned, reduced sodium, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans are a ready‑to‑eat vegetable that has been heat‑processed and sealed in a can with reduced sodium. A vegetable oil is added, but the specific type of fat is not specified (NS). The beans retain most of their nutrients, have a tender texture, and a mildly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans belong to the legume family and are rich in protein and fiber.
Canning allows the beans to be stored for several years without loss of flavor.
Reduced sodium is achieved by replacing part of the salt with other flavor enhancers.
Added oil improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K.
In the US and Canada, canned green beans are often used in ready‑made dishes such as chili and stews.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports normal digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A is essential for vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K plays a role in blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt content is beneficial for blood pressure management.

items.title: Added plant fats
items.content: The added oil aids the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and provides energy.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beans.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The product contains added fats, which may be undesirable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Bacterial contamination after opening
items.content: Once the can is opened, store the beans in the refrigerator and consume within a few days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Green beans can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, stews, or used as a side dish. Before serving, drain the liquid and, if desired, rinse with cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Dried mango are slices of ripe mango that have been dehydrated to a low moisture level. They retain a bright orange color, sweet tropical aroma, and characteristic flavor, but have a denser, chewy texture. Dried mango are commonly enjoyed as a snack and added to granola, baked goods, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried mango can contain up to 30 % natural sugars, making them sweet without added sugar.
Mango belongs to the Anacardiaceae family and is a relative of papaya and avocado.
Tropical regions of Asia, Africa, and South America are the main producers of dried mango.
Dried fruits are popular in backpacking meals because they store well without refrigeration.
Beta‑carotene gives mango its vivid color and supports eye health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Dried mango provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene, a provitamin A, helps maintain healthy skin and vision.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal heart function and fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Because of natural sugars, dried mango can raise blood glucose levels; people with diabetes should limit portions.

items.title: Mango allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sulfite content
items.content: Sulfites are sometimes added for preservation and can cause reactions in sulfite‑sensitive persons.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Dried mango can be mildly acidic; excessive consumption may cause stomach discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried mango can be eaten straight from the pack, tossed into granola, yogurt, smoothies, baked goods, salads, or used in Asian dishes such as curries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried mango in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator, where they retain flavor and chewiness for up to 12 months.

sports-drink-dry-concentrate-not-reconst.title: Sports drink, dry concentrate, not reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: The dry concentrate sports drink is designed for rapid energy and electrolyte replenishment after intense training. It does not require reconstitution, making it convenient where water is unavailable.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The concentrate contains over 30 % carbohydrates in the form of fast‑absorbing sugars.
It includes electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium) in an optimal ratio to reduce cramp risk.
The product is free from artificial colors and flavors.
Packaging is made of aluminum foil, providing a long shelf life without quality loss.
Dry concentrate is easy to transport and store even under extreme temperatures.

items.title: Rapid energy replenishment
items.content: High simple‑carbohydrate content delivers an immediate glucose boost, supporting performance.

items.title: Electrolyte balance restoration
items.content: Sodium and potassium help maintain fluid‑electrolyte equilibrium, reducing dehydration risk.

items.title: Muscle recovery support
items.content: Magnesium participates in protein synthesis and muscle relaxation after exertion.

items.title: Endurance enhancement
items.content: The combination of carbs and electrolytes enables longer workouts without a sudden energy drop.

items.title: No extra calories from fat
items.content: The concentrate contains no fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High levels of simple sugars may be unsuitable for individuals with diabetes or glucose sensitivity.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The product may contain trace amounts of dairy or soy, which should be considered by allergic persons.

items.title: Excess sodium intake
items.content: Overconsumption can lead to elevated blood pressure in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Not for children under 12
items.content: Due to high sugar and electrolyte concentration, it is recommended for adults and adolescents only.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume the concentrate directly from the packet or dispenser, optionally sipping a small amount of water to ease swallowing. Recommended dose is 10 g before training and 10 g after.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the package tightly sealed to prevent moisture absorption.
